quotes.summary_phrase: Reflecting on the societal shifts and lessons from the pandemic
quotes.excerpt: I don't know if we've taken fully the lessons that we all probably learned there.
quotes.quote: Anything that helped us get out of what we all were dealing with, that brought, I think, that was connecting people to something and things, I think was healing. I don't know if we've taken fully the lessons that we all probably learned there. We may have got Mr. Miyagi by it all, like the pandemic, and like we won't realize it till two minutes before we all die that we're like, oh, that's what the pandemic was. But look at the individual good things that happened. They weren't self-dealing. They were like, okay, I got to get this out of me. Whatever this is, I got to connect with people that I have connections with, and then people wanted that connection.

quotes.excerpt: Once they knew that we weren't coming over there to fuck around with them, they welcomed us.
quotes.quote: I remember this one British guy after we had done the second commercial, we're doing a thing for, I think for Steve Nash's foundation, like before the where we played Coach Lasso and Coach Beard, and coached his foundation like his charity game. quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Using FIFA video games to develop ideas for Ted Lasso
quotes.excerpt: I used Man City on FIFA, where a lot of the ideas for football came from.
quotes.quote: I used Man City on FIFA, where a lot of the ideas for football came from. I'd sit there during the pandemic, smoking weed and drinking micheladas, and kept a little yellow pad. I bought Xboxes for everybody, and we got the codes out. This is before the show had even come out. We gave it to all the dudes that played on the team, so we could all connect over the things. We had dudes playing in Mexico, Paris, and it was pro clubs, so you would have up to sometimes 10 or 11 dudes playing all at once, and I'd keep this pad next to me, if someone said something funny or some interesting or just triggered a thought, I'd write that down.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Focusing on personal creative standards rather than external validation
quotes.excerpt: Do I like the way we went about making it? Want to be proud of that.
quotes.quote: You always believe in what you're doing. I didn't think anybody was going to like it. I mean, I knew I liked it. That's all you can do. Is like, do I like it? Do I like the way we went about making it? Want to be proud of that, proud of what we make, proud of how we make it. That's all you have control over. I remember that John Wooden quote, don't concern yourself over which things you have no control. I believe in that. That's the only way to do it. Because people will find you, especially this day and age.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: The therapeutic nature of writing and collaborating in a writers room
quotes.excerpt: It almost becomes therapeutic where you start to recognize the things that you probably were thinking yourself
quotes.quote: Reps. Every week, especially as a writer, you're writing and producing. You're attaching a talent, whoever's hosting, Dwayne Johnson, Scarlett Johansson, etc., you're trying to write a scene where you score, where they score, where they don't feel they're being outshown. Or then you're sitting in a room with writers and you're having these conversations about your lives. It almost becomes therapeutic where you start to recognize the things that you probably were thinking yourself quietly, they're saying out loud, so it gives you the strength to say it out loud yourself and you realize how much more similar we are than we are different.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Creating Ted Lasso as a form of personal wish fulfillment
quotes.excerpt: It is very, very personal, and I'm glad it happened later in my life
quotes.quote: It's the wish fulfillment of getting to play a coach that I'd never had specifically, but always wish I had or wish I could be, the dad I wish I could be, the brother I wish I could be, the teammate. You try to put all that in there. So, it is very, very personal, and I'm glad it happened later in my life, because if it would have happened early in my life, I'd be an asshole. I wouldn't know how to handle it.
